findings.text: The first paragraph tells a newcomer what Athena is, who it is for and what problem it solves. That covers 'what is it' and 'why does it matter' within a few seconds of reading.
findings.source: Athena is an open-source system, written in Rust, that turns a short request into a change to a code repository. ... It solves the problem of AI edits that arrive unreviewed and unaccountable.

findings.text: The headline is about a different project, firstmate. A newcomer visiting Athena's site sees a title about firstmate's work handling, not about Athena.

The second section is a failure message showing internal job ids. It fails to show the 'models, verdict and costs' the first paragraph promises. This harms first impressions and leaves Athena's main claim without proof.
findings.source: Check it on a real job: "The records of job 20261029-073603-7kqv could not be read here, so no models, verdict or costs are shown: no reading record for job 20261029-073603-7kqv."

findings.text: The next steps are concrete and complete: what to install first, the clone and setup commands, and a first command to try. A newcomer knows what to do next, and a link near the top jumps straight here.
findings.source: Next steps: "Before installing, have git 2.40 or later, a C linker, curl, and either Claude Code or npm ... ./setup.sh ... athena ask "add a changelog""

findings.text: Most of the page is a detailed description of how firstmate works (exit codes, place counters, pending-close replays). It shows how carefully Athena traces its claims, but a newcomer trying to understand Athena must scroll past it all to find the next steps.
findings.source: Sections States of a piece of work, Counters, Transitions (t1–t12), Why it is built this way, Glossary, Claims and sources (c1–c45)

findings.text: The page explains why it is a study of firstmate: it is a demonstration of Athena. Without this sentence the long middle would be confusing.
findings.source: A study is Athena's written reading of another software project, taken at one fixed commit ... with every statement traced to a claim, and every claim to lines in the project's own files.

findings.text: This link is meant for the site owner, yet it sits in the header that every newcomer sees. A newcomer cannot tell whether it applies to them.
findings.source: Owner view: proposals waiting for your decision.

findings.text: This section and the footer describe internal repository layout. That means nothing to a first-time visitor and does not help them.
findings.source: About this page: "This page's study id, firstmate-work-handling, is the name of the folder under studies/ that holds the data this page is generated from."

findings.text: The target user is stated clearly. But no example output of a real Athena run is shown anywhere, so a newcomer has to take on trust what they would get back.
findings.source: It is for people who want to give a lazy, one- or two-line request and get back a commit they can trace to the request, the models, the cost and the verdict.
